«*è morta nella sua propria casa **ANNA FALCO, di mesi TREDICI**, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina, domiciliata ivi, **figlia di MICHELANGELO FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, **e di MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*» — died **4 May 1831** at thirteen hours, thirteen months old, so born about **April 1830**. **Verified from the image, work-list row 58.** **THE CITATION POINTED AT IMAGE 19 RIGHT, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT CHILD** — Carmina Maccaniello, ten months, daughter of Pasquale Maccaniello and Raffaela Zimbardo, dead on 28 April. **The act is on IMAGE 20 RIGHT**, found by sweeping the volume's date lines. **AND IT SHARPENS THE QUESTION RAISED ELSEWHERE TODAY.** This archive now holds **two Anna Falco, three years apart, each «figlia di MICHELANGELO FALCO», with two different mothers**: this one **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, and the Anna of 16 March 1834 **RAFFAELA FALCO**. **A remarriage between them is excluded** if this Mariantonia Vigliotta is the woman who was still bearing children to a Michele Falco in 1834, 1836 and 1842 and whom he survived in 1850. **So either there are two Michelangelo Falco at Arienzo, or one of the two mothers is misread.** Both mothers have now been read from the image at full resolution. **Neither reading is in doubt; the identification is.** **And the declarant is the reason this household is kin at all**: «*e **VINCENZO FALCO**, di anni **trentotto**, di professione contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, **PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA***», where **ANDREA CRISCI, fifty-eight**, beside him is only «**VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA**». **The clerk drew the distinction himself, in one sentence.** Read from the image on 20 September 2026.

**THIS CHILD IS NOT RECORDED AS THIS COUPLE'S, AND THE ROW IS LEFT STANDING RATHER THAN DELETED.** Until 20 September 2026 an **ANNA FALCO, eight days old, dead 7 March 1834** stood here as a daughter of Michelangelo Falco and **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**. **The act was found and read.** It is act 16, image 11 left, of **16 March 1834**, and it says «*figlia di **MICHELANGELO FALCO** … e di **RAFFAELA FALCO***». **The mother is not Mariantonia Vigliotta.** **So she is published under MICHELANGELO FALCO & RAFFAELA FALCO instead**, and whether that Michelangelo is this one — widowed and remarried — or a second man of the name is an open question this archive does not close by assuming.

THE WORD IS «ZIO», NOT «VICINO», AND THIS ARCHIVE READ IT WRONG. Re-read 16 Sep 2026 at full magnification: the word before «del defunto» is three letters, written twice, and it is not the six-letter «vicino» the same clerk writes on the 1823 and 1825 acts of this same household — those two acts are the control, and they are in this file to be checked against. So the register states in 1824 that the dead child's mother MARIA FALCO is kin to these two men, four years before the 1828 act on which this archive had rested that conclusion. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE. Read strictly, «zio del defunto» makes Maria Falco a SISTER of Pasquale (bapt. 24 October 1767) and of Giuseppe — and therefore a daughter of MATTEO FALCO and FRANCESCA CRISCI. Her own stated age forbids it: twenty-five in June 1824, born about 1799, when Francesca Crisci was bearing children by 1767. Either that age is one of this register's inventions — and this archive holds the same clerk making Giuseppe Falco forty and forty-five four days apart — or «zio» is doing the loose collateral work that «parente» does in 1828. THE WORD IS RECORDED AND THE PEDIGREE IS REFUSED. THE ONLY RECORD IN WHICH PASQUALE FALCO ACTS FOR HIMSELF, and the only document in this archive written in his own hand: the act closes «segnato da noi e da uno de' dichiaranti, avendo l'altro cioè GIUSEPPE FALCO dichiarato di non sapere scrivere per non averlo mai imparato», and beneath it, in a slow upright hand quite unlike the clerk's, stands the signature «PASCALE FALCO» — the Neapolitan form, without the qu, the way he said his own name. His brother could not sign. He is fifty-five here, one year out against his baptism of 24 October 1767 — ordinary — and his trade is COLONO, a tenant farmer, where his death act of 1834 calls him contadino.

evidence: THE DATE OF A MARRIAGE THIS ARCHIVE HELD ONLY AS A FACT. The 1818 Tavola Alfabetica annuale de' Matrimonj pairs «ARCANGELO COSSI» with «ANNA FALCO», her parents given as «DI PASQUALE, e CHIARA RIVETTI» — no «fu» before either, and Pasquale Falco did not die until 1834. THE SURNAME IS WRITTEN COSSI HERE AND CRISCI IN THE 1820 ACTS — both read from the image, and this archive has already recorded that Cossi and Crisci are not reliably separable in this hand. The identification does not rest on it: there is one Anna Falco of Pasquale and Chiara, and one Arcangelo she was married to

evidence: THE ACT THAT LIFTS A REFUSAL THIS ARCHIVE MADE ON PURPOSE. «3. FALCO ANGELANDREA | Arienzo | FALCO VINCENZO, e CRISCI ANDREANA» ed «CIMMINO MARIA | Arienzo | CIMMINO ALESSANDRO, e SOLLI [ROSA]», the church date given as «**29 MARZO**» [1847] — READ AGAIN 20 Sep 2026 at 3,000 px, where the second digit carries a full descender loop; the act number **4** two rows above it on the same page has none. This archive published it as «24 MARZO». When Angelandrea's birth act of 12 September 1826 was published, it was DELIBERATELY NOT JOINED to «the ANGELO Falco who married Maria Cimmino in 1847 or the ANDREA Falco who married Maria Carmela», because the household held all three names and each of the other two was known only from a parish marriage act. THE CIVIL INDEX SETTLES ONE HALF: the man who married MARIA CIMMINO, daughter of Alessandro and Rosa Solli, is written ANGELANDREA — the exact name of the 1826 birth act — so ANGELO of the parish act and ANGELANDREA of the birth act are ONE MAN, married at TWENTY. The ANDREA who married Maria Carmela, daughter of Onofrio and Angela Imbimbo, REMAINS A SEPARATE SON and is still not joined to anything. DATE DISCREPANCY RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED: this tavola gives the church wedding as 24 March 1847 and the parish record held here gives 17 April 1847 — the same kind of civil-versus-parish disagreement already documented for Raffaele Falco's marriage of 1844

evidence: A FALCO HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER SEEN. «8. LUIGI FALCO | Arienzo | Di SEBASTIANO, e COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO» ed «GIUSTINA PETRILLO | Arienzo | Fu SABATINO, e BRIGIDA COSSI | A 19 detto [1815]». NEITHER SEBASTIANO FALCO NOR COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THIS ARCHIVE — not in the households, not in the register, not in the people file. NOT THE LUIGI FALCO OF STRADA CAMELLARA, who was baptised in December 1819 to Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci and could not marry in 1815. NO KINSHIP TO THIS LINE IS CLAIMED. Recorded because the archive's standing position is that the surname identifies nobody, and the way to hold that position is to name the other houses rather than ignore them **THE ACT ITSELF WAS READ ON 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND IT DISAGREES WITH THE INDEX ABOUT HER FORENAME.** «*L'anno milleottocento quindici, a' dì DICIANNOVE del mese di MARZO, alle ore tredici … è comparso LUIGI FALCO di anni DICIOTTO COMPITI, di professione SAPUNARO, domiciliato nel comune de' SEI CASALI, strada CROCE DI SAN FELICE, MINORE, assistito da SEBASTIANO FALCO suo padre della stessa professione e domicilio, e da COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO sua madre di anni CINQUANTACINQUE, di professione FILATRICE … È comparsa egualmente STELLA PETRILLO di anni DICIOTTO, domiciliata in questa suddetta comune, STRADA DEL BORGO, di professione FILATRICE, MINORE, assistita da BRIGIDA COSSI sua madre di anni CINQUANTASEI, di professione contadina, domiciliata colla figlia, essendo morto il padre SABBATINO PETRILLO*». **The parents match the index exactly, so the woman is the same; the forename does not.** The act reads **STELLA**, the index reads **GIULIA**, and this archive had published **«Giustina»**, which is neither. evidence: «ARCANGELO, e SARA RUGGIERO» — SARA, not ROSA. The archive's only previous source for this woman is the parish marriage act, whose machine transcript gives «e [ROSAE] Ruggiero» WITH THE FORENAME IN BRACKETS, the archive's own mark for a reading it did not trust. The civil index is unambiguous. AND IT EXPLAINS A NAME: the daughter born to this couple on 19 DECEMBER 1828 was called SARA — the only Sara in the household, and this archive found her only yesterday. She was named for her mother's mother. The midwife who declared that birth was GELSOMINA RUGGIERO, sixty, and a Gelsomina Ruggiero stood MATRINA at this couple's son Raffaele's baptism in 1818; the Ruggiero kinship is now MORE likely and is STILL NOT CLAIMED

evidence: READ FROM THE IMAGE AT LAST, and the machine transcript was right. «Anno Domini 1841 die vero 27. NOVEMBRIS obiit JOANNES FALCO filius JOSEPHI et ANTONIAE DI GUIDA, aetate sua ANNORUM 24 CIRCITER, omnibus Sacramentis munitus et in commendatione animae adjutus, cujus cadaver IN SODALITATE S. MARIAE GRATIARUM jacet» — the margin gives the Italian form, GIOVANNI FALCO. THE «24 CIRCITER» IS CONFIRMED, so this man was born about 1817 and CANNOT be DON GIOVANNI FALCO the deacon, whose birth of 6 April 1825 is fixed by his civil act AND his parish baptism and who died in 1849. THIS HOUSEHOLD HAD TWO LIVING SONS NAMED GIOVANNI between 1825 and 1841, which the archive's necronym rule does not explain: the elder was alive when the younger was named. HE DIED FORTIFIED WITH ALL THE SACRAMENTS, which the register does not say of everyone. AND THERE IS NO CIVIL DEATH ACT FOR HIM — all ninety acts of the Arienzo 1841 death register were read on 14 September 2026 and hold no Falco at all

A confraternity buried many families and this is NOT offered as evidence of kinship; it is recorded because the archive holds only two burials with a named place and both are in this one

«…è morto nella sua propria casa DON GIOVANNI FALCO, nato in Arienzo, di anni VENTICINQUE, di professione DIACONO … figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO di professione COLONO … e di ANTONIA DI GUIDA» — 26 November 1849, ore ventidue. THE ONLY MAN IN THIS FAMILY KNOWN TO HAVE TAKEN ORDERS, from a household of contadini on strada Camellara. Born 6 April 1825 by both his civil act and his parish baptism, so he was TWENTY-FOUR YEARS AND SEVEN MONTHS, and the act rounds it to twenty-five. NOT the Giovanni Falco of this house who was buried on 27 November 1841 «annorum 24 circiter» — two brothers of one name, alive together for sixteen years. The declarants are GENNARO CIOFFI, 52, and FRANCESCO CIOFFI, 56, both contadini of strada Camellara. The act also keeps GIUSEPPE FALCO ALIVE in November 1849 at about seventy, with no «fu» before his name. evidence: A FOURTH CHILD FOR THE FIRST-COUSIN MARRIAGE, and the third of them to die small. «71. FALCO PASQUALE | Arienzo | contadino | FALCO FRANCESCO, e FALCO RAFFAELA | A 30 detto [OTTOBRE] 1838» — the row above it is dated 10 Ottobre, which fixes the month. FROM THE MARGIN OF HIS OWN BIRTH ACT, not from any marriage register: «*Con atto **6 agosto 1856** at[to] **21** in **S[?] …a Vico** il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI** [di] **Gaspare**(?)*». **THE COMUNE IS NOT ESTABLISHED.** At five times magnification the place reads «*S[?]basia a Vico*» and resolves no further. **SANTA MARIA A VICO IS THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE AND IS EXCLUDED BY ITS OWN REGISTER**: `an_ua55736`, *Matrimoni* 1856, **act 21 is Don Domenico de Lucia, 29, of San Felice, promised 14 June 1856** — no Falco, and no act of 6 August (act 31 is 3 August, act 32 is 9 August). **What is certain is the annotation itself**: a Falco of this house married a DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI on 6 August 1856, recorded as act 21 somewhere «…a Vico». The bride's father reads **Gaspare** rather than the Giuseppe first published. Note that the groom's own mother is a **VIGLIOTTA**; whether the two families are one is NOT established. **IT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS ARCHIVE USED A BIRTH-ACT MARGIN AS A SOURCE**, and the rule it produced — that a civil birth act can carry the child's later marriage, in another comune, where no local register shows it — has since found Pasqua Falco's marriage of 1880, Giovanna Arricale's of 1872 and **both** of Domenica Falco's, of 1874 and 1881.

MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA, and on STRADA CAMELLARA — this archive has the household at STRADA COSTA in 1816. Either they moved, or the street is not the identifier here. He is NOT the Giuseppe Falco of the same street who declared a birth seven months later: that one is a CONTADINO married to ANTONIA DI GUIDA. Two Giuseppe Falco on one street in one year, separated by trade and by wife.
Alive and bearing a child on 18 March 1819, three days after burying two. Her age is given in this act; it is recorded rather than relied on.

THE CIVIL ACT BEHIND A BAPTISM THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD — not a new child. Act 133: «è comparso VINCENZO FALCO, di anni VENTISEI, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo comune, STRADA CAMELLARA … ad ore dieci è nato nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante e da ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legitima d'Anni VENTIDUE, un MASCHIO … a cui si è dato il nome di LUIGI». The parish entry gave only «Dec 1819» and «nominatus est Aloysius»; this gives the day, the hour, the street and both parents' ages. **ACT NUMBER CORRECTED 20 Sep 2026, from 133 to 134.** The leaf reference was right and the number was not: image 71 left is headed «*Numero d'ordine **CENTOTRENTAQUATTRO***». **Act 133 is on the facing leaf, image 70 right, and it is a different family — «*è comparso **VINCENZO MAURO**, di anni ventisette, di professione viaticale, domiciliato in questo comune strada Sant'Andrea … da **ANDREANA CARFORA** sua moglie legittima, d'anni ventisei, un Maschio***». **Same day, same clerk, a Vincenzo and an Andreana in each** — which is exactly the kind of neighbour an archive chasing act 133 would have taken for its own.

«di anni VENTISEI» — twenty-six. He was given as TWENTY-SEVEN on 10 May 1818, nineteen months earlier: HE GETS YOUNGER BY A YEAR WHILE NINETEEN MONTHS PASS. His baptism of 1 February 1792 makes him twenty-seven here, so both civil figures are wrong and the register is the reason the archive dates him from the font instead.

«d'Anni VENTIDUE» — twenty-two, so b. c.1797. This is the Andreana Crisci who married Vincenzo Falco in December 1814, on his own street and in his own house; she is not the other Andreana Crisci this archive keeps separate.

THE CIVIL ACT BEHIND THE CHURCH DATE, AND IT DATES HIS BIRTH. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **CRESCENZO FALCO maggiore di anni VENTICINQUE nato in ARIENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **IVI strada Sant'Andrea**, figlio di **GIUSEPPE FALCO** di professione simile domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** di professione contadina domiciliata **ivi***» — TRANSCRIPTION CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive wrote «domiciliato **in** strada Sant'Andrea» and the act reads «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea». The dropped word matters, because «ivi» in these forms means THE COMUNE and not the street — the bride in this very act is «domiciliata **ivi strada Cappuccini**», one word and two streets. So GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA are recorded here as domiciled AT ARIENZO, and THE ACT DOES NOT GIVE THEIR STREET. Anything this archive concluded about the household leaving strada Camellara rests on a word that was never there — bride **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, 23, contadina, of strada Cappuccini, «*figlia di **GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO** … e di **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE** … **defunta***». The INDICAZIONE records the church celebration: **3 February 1845**, parish of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, witnesses **Luigi Verdicchio** and **Nunzio Rivetti**. TWENTY-FIVE ON 2 FEBRUARY 1845 puts his birth between 3 February 1819 and 2 February 1820 — and his civil birth act is 11 October 1819. **RE-READ IN FULL, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58 — and one thing in it was nearly "corrected" and is right.** The act says «**maggiore** di anni venticinque», and «maggiore di anni X» is elsewhere a statement of legal majority, not of age; on that reading the act would bound his birth on one side only and «it dates his birth» would be false. **The control is four lines below, in the same sentence: the bride is «maggiore di anni VENTITRE».** No age of majority is twenty-three. **So «maggiore» is a status and the number is the age**, for both of them, and the inference stands. Everything else verifies: act 3, «Domenico Zinelli Sindaco», Arienzo, **distretto di CASERTA**, ore ventuno; «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea»; the church celebration on **3 February** before **LUIGI VERDICCHIO** and **NUNZIO RIVETTI**.

Given with a trade and a domicile and NOT marked «defunto» — in an act that marks BOTH of the bride's parents dead in the same sentence. He was already known alive in November 1849 from his son the deacon's death act; this is an independent sighting on a form that states death explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

HER LATEST DATED SIGHTING BY TWENTY-FIVE YEARS. This archive held her on one dated document — her son Crescenzo's birth act of 11 October 1819. Here she is «*di professione contadina domiciliata ivi*», alive, in an act that writes «DEFUNTO» and «DEFUNTA» for the bride's father and mother. HER DEATH HAS BEEN HUNTED THROUGH THE PARISH REGISTER AND NOT FOUND; the window now opens on 2 February 1845 instead of October 1819.

Crescenzo Falco's bride: twenty-three, contadina, born in Arienzo, and an orphan — «*figlia di GENNARO MORGILLO defunto, di professione colono … e di MARIA FELICIA SANSONE, di professione contadina … defunta*». The church act carries a dispensation «*super quarto gradu consanguinitatis*», so she and Crescenzo were third cousins.

HER SECOND MARRIAGE, FROM THE MARGIN OF HER OWN BIRTH ACT — a document written fifty-seven years before it. «*A 30 Dic.re 1880 l'Uf.le dello Stato Civile d'**ARIENZO** sposò **PASQUA FALCO** con **PASQUALE CARFORA*** — 27 Agosto 1881». She married **ANGELO MAJONE on 9 September 1856** at thirty-three; this makes her **fifty-seven** and, on the ordinary reading, a widow of Majone. THE ANNOTATION SITS ON ACT 38 OF 1823, her own — born 30 March 1823 to Giuseppe Falco, «*il nome di PASQUA*» — so the identification is physical rather than inferred. **CARFORA is a surname this archive hunts elsewhere** — Maria Carfora of Forchia, generation seven's grandmother, whose parents remain unreachable. **Pasquale Carfora is NOT claimed as kin to her**: the name is dense at Forchia and present at Arienzo, and nothing here joins them.
Alive and marrying at fifty-seven. This archive's latest dated sighting of her had been her first wedding in 1856.

NAMED ONLY BY HIS DAUGHTER'S MARRIAGE, and already dead when it happened: «*figlia di **GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO**, di professione **colono***». Not claimed as kin — recorded because the Falco married the Morgillo repeatedly and this archive cannot yet tell those Morgillo houses apart. **A CANDIDATE FOR HIS DEATH ACT, FOUND ON 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 IN THE ARCHIVE'S OWN FILES.** Arienzo Morti 1843, act 33 — `an_ua14345` img24R — records **GENNARO MORGILLO, fifty-three, COLONO of strada Camellara, «vedovo di Felicia S___», son of ANGELO MORGILLO defunto, colono**, dead **4 August 1843**. That is eighteen months before this marriage, it agrees on the trade, on the wife's forename and on her being dead first, and the bride's **strada Cappuccini** is the hill where that Angelo Morgillo's house stood. **It is graded PROBABLE and no more**, because Morgillo is the commonest surname in these registers. **AND THE WIFE'S SURNAME NOW AGREES TOO.** The 1843 word was published as «Sompone» and read on 20 September as **«Sanſone»** — SANSONE — against a control on the same street: Arienzo Morti 1826 act 22, declared by **ANGELO SANSONE** of strada Camellara, whose surname is written in the same hand-shape, long ſ and all. **What this archive had taken for a «p» is a long s.** So the mother named here is the woman named there. **The 1845 processetto would settle it in one line**, by quoting the death act's number.

«*e di **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE**, di professione **contadina** … **defunta***» — from her daughter's marriage act of 2 February 1845. **PUBLISHED HERE AS «SANSONE» UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND WITH IT THE CLAIM THAT THE SURNAME «HAD NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE AT ALL».** The letter is a long **ſ**, not a **z**, and the test is on the same leaf: **«Crescenzo», in the groom's own name, has a z** — a compact loop that drops below the line and has no ascender. **The letter in this surname rises above the x-height before it descends.** A z in this hand does not do that. **So the surname was not new.** **ANGELO SANSONE**, contadino of **strada Camellara**, declares the death of Maria Falco, wife of Alfonso Diglio, on 25 April 1826 — and his surname is written in the same shape. **Three acts now agree: 1826, 1843 and 1845, all SANSONE.** Not claimed as kin.

Twenty-three, contadina, born in Arienzo, and an orphan of both parents when she married **CRESCENZO FALCO**. The church act carries a dispensation «*super quarto gradu consanguinitatis*», so she and her husband were third cousins — the fourth Falco marriage inside the fourth degree this archive holds.

«*il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI** [di] **Gaspare**(?)*» — from the margin of her husband's birth act. **Her father's forename was first published as Giuseppe and re-reads as GASPARE at five times magnification; neither is certain.** **And the comune is not established**: Santa Maria a Vico, the obvious candidate, is excluded by its own 1856 register, whose act 21 is a de Lucia. Nothing else about her is known. **AND A REFUSAL THAT BELONGS BESIDE HER.** The groom's own mother is a **VIGLIOTTA**. **Whether Vigliotti and Vigliotta are one family here is NOT established, and nothing in this margin joins them.** (Written into `data/households.tsv` and not into the file the site builds from; recovered by work-list row 75.)

«*l'Uf.le dello Stato Civile d'Arienzo sposò PASQUA FALCO con **PASQUALE CARFORA***» — her second husband, married when she was fifty-seven. **NOT claimed as kin to the Carfora of Forchia** whom this archive hunts elsewhere; the surname is common in both towns and nothing joins them.

THE CONTROL THAT SEPARATES THE TWO SURNAMES. «*è comparso **FRANCESCO COSSI**, di anni **trenta**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in detto comune, **strada COSSI***» — the same word twice in one sentence, as a name and as a street, which checks the reading with no judgement at all. Thirty in 1819, so b. c.1789. **The strada Camellara FRANCESCO CIOFFI is twenty-seven in 1824, b. c.1797. Different men, different ages, different streets.** Not kin to the Falco; recorded to hold the two families apart.

«*e da **TERESA MORGILLO** sua moglie legitima d'anni **ventotto***» — twenty-eight, so b. c.1791. She is the wife of the strada Cossi Francesco, NOT of the strada Camellara Francesco Cioffi, whose wife is **MARIA FALCO**.

THE ACT THAT JOINS TWO HOUSEHOLDS THIS ARCHIVE KEPT APART. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **MICHELE FALCO maggiore, di anni QUARANTATRE, nato in ARIENZO, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO DEFUNTO**, di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, e di **CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**, di professione filatrice … **VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI** … e **GIOVANNA D'AMBROGIO MAGGIORE, di anni TRENOVE**, di professione contadina*». **HER AGE IS THIRTY-NINE, NOT NINETEEN** — re-read at the leaf's full 3,200 pixels on 20 September 2026. The numeral's initial is a tall ascender crossed by a diagonal, a **t**; this hand's **d**, in «CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA» four lines above it in the same pen, is a small closed bowl. «Trenove» is the clerk's contraction of *trentanove*. **And the act says so twice**: she is «MAGGIORE», of age, and no consent of her mother is taken — a nineteen-year-old would have been «MINORE», as Andreana Crisci is in 1814. So she was born about **1811**, not about 1831. **«Michele Falco & Antonia Vigliotta» and «Michele Falco & Maria Giovanna d'Ambrogio» are ONE MAN AND TWO MARRIAGES.** The d'Ambrogio household was known only by a daughter **Antonia born 19 November 1850** — nine months after this wedding. **Verified against the image, work-list row 58 — act 6, and every word holds.** «*L'anno mille ottocento **cinquanta**, il dì **dodici** del mese di **Febrajo**, alle ore **sedici**, avanti di Noi **ARCANGELO DE FUSCO Sindaco***». **The bride's parents had never been recorded here**: **DOMENICO D'AMBROGIO defunto**, contadino, and **CARMINA MANNA**, **filatrice**, and she is of **strada Sant'Andrea**. The church celebration followed the same day at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, before **ALFONSO VERDICCHIO** and a **CLEMENTE MOR[GILLO]**. **THE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, 20 September 2026, AND THEY ARE TWO MEN.** The 1828 marriage index was read from the image at last: «*10. **FALCO MICHELANGELO** | Arienzo | **FALCO PASQUALE, e RIVETTI CHIARA*** … ***VIGLIOTTI ANTONIA** | ivi | **VIGLIOTTI FRANCESCO, e REPETELLI VITTORIA*** … **Xbre 1828**». And the 1850 act's father was magnified for the first time: «*figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO Defunto***», a capital **R**. **MICHELANGELO FALCO is a son of PASQUALE. MICHELE FALCO is a son of RAFFAELE.** Two fathers, two men — **and both of them married a woman called ANTONIA VIGLIOTTI.** That coincidence is now documented from two marriage records rather than guessed at, and it is what had the two households tangled together.

«*VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI*» — she was dead by 12 February 1850. Her daughter Chiara died in 1846 aged seven and her daughter Carmela on 4 August 1859, which is AFTER this date and therefore a child of the first marriage buried nine years into the second.

MICHELE FALCO'S FATHER, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME: «*figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO DEFUNTO**, di professione **simile** [colono], domiciliato **ivi** [strada Camellara]*». A generation this archive did not have for this house. NOT joined to the direct line's Raffaele Falco of 1818, who was thirty-one and alive in 1850.

«*e di **CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**, di professione **filatrice***». **A NAME THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAS, AND THIS IS ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT HER.** Generation two's wife CHIARA RIVETTI was the widow of **PASQUALE** Falco, died 13 September 1843 aged eighty, and bore Pasquale children from 1789 to 1802 — so she cannot have been married to a Raffaele Falco when this Michele was born about 1807. **Either a second Chiara Rivetti, on a street where the Rivetti are dense, or Michele's stated age is badly wrong. Nothing is merged and nothing is chosen.**

NINETEEN, contadina, marrying a widower of forty-three. She is the «Maria Giovanna d'Ambrosio» of the household this archive recorded separately from the Vigliotta one; **the 1859 death index clipped her name, and this act gives it whole.** Her daughter Antonia was born 19 November 1850, nine months later.

READ FROM THE IMAGE — this record was a FamilySearch index stub («Entry for Luigi Falco and Vincenzo Falco») until 16 September 2026. Arienzo *Morti 1864*, **atto 91**: «*…è morto nella sua casa **LUIGI FALCO = MARITO DI CAROLINA CIMMINO** — nato in **Arienzo**, di anni **QUARANTUNO**, di professione **INDUSTRIANTE**, domiciliato **Contrada Capodiconca**, figlio di **VINCENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **alla CAMELLARA**, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata ivi*». Declared by **Fabrizio Crisci**, 62, *cantiniere*, and **Francesco di Lucia**, 40, *trainante*, both of Capodiconca. **HE WAS MARRIED**, which this archive did not know, and **he had left strada Camellara** — an *industriante* of Capodiconca while his father was still a *colono* of Camellara. **The stated age is wrong by three**: born 21 December 1819, he died five days short of forty-five and the act says forty-one. **VERIFIED AGAINST THE IMAGE, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58 — and the act number was the folio.** This page cited **atto 47**; **47 is the figure stamped in the leaf's margin**, and the act is headed «**Num. d'ordine 91**». The facing page of the same opening is **«Num. d'ordine 92»**, which settles it. **The stamped figure in this volume counts pages, not acts** — the same trap the 1820 death register set, where folio 5 carries act 6 and folio 25 carries act 47. **One quotation is tightened.** The act writes «*e di **ANDREA CRISCI**, domiciliata ivi*» — the clerk drops the **-na**. This archive quoted «ANDREANA CRISCI» inside the guillemets. **The woman is the same and the guillemets are for what is written.**

«*MARITO DI **CAROLINA CIMMINO***» — Luigi Falco's widow, and a person this archive did not know existed. Nothing else about her is established: no marriage act, no parents, no age. **The Arienzo civil marriage record is complete 1809–1858 and holds no Falco–Cimmino wedding**, so they married after 1858 or not at Arienzo.

GENERATION THREE, ALIVE AT SEVENTY-TWO — twenty years later than any sighting this archive had. «*figlio di **VINCENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **alla Camellara***», with **no «fu» and no «defunto»**. **THE FORM MARKS THE DEAD AND THIS REGISTER USES IT**: on the same opening, act 41 gives «*figlio di **fu** Nicola … e della **fu** Colomba Capezzo*», act 43 «*figlia del **fu** Giuseppe … e della **fu** Cecilia Silvestri*», act 45 «*figlia del **fu** Don Stefano … e della **fu** Donna Faustina Cimmino*», act 49 «*figlio del **fu** Filippo … e della **fu** Lucrezia Varrecchia*». Four dead parents marked on one sheet, and these two not. His baptism of 1 February 1792 makes him seventy-two.
«*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***» — alive, unmarked, on the same evidence as her husband. Her latest previous sighting was her son Raffaele's marriage act of 7 March 1844.

**THE MARRIAGE, FOUND** — this archive held the household from its children alone. **RE-READ IN FULL FROM THE IMAGE, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58**, and the reading below replaces one that put a «fu» in front of four names the act never puts one in front of. «*L'anno mille ottocento **sessanta**, il dì **VENTUNO** di **Gennajo**, alle ore ventitre, avanti di Noi **Stefano Sargenti**, uffiziale dello Stato Civile di **ARIENZO**, distretto di **CASERTA** … sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO**, di anni **trentaquattro**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **Forchia**, figlio di **CARMINE ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **ROSA CEGLIA defunta** … e **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA**, di anni **ventinove**, nata in **ARIENZO**, domiciliata in Arienzo, figlia di **VALERIO CARFORA**, di professione contadino, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **PASQUA MORGILLO defunta***». **THREE THINGS CHANGE.** The act is of **21 January**, not the twentieth — «*il dì **ventuno***». The groom's own spelling is **SABBATINO**, with two b. And **the bride's father is not marked dead**: see Valerio Carfora below. The church celebration followed on **22 January**, before witnesses read here as **PASQUALE LAUDATO** and **ANTONIO CRISCI** — the last surname is **Crisci**, with no descender, and was published as «Crispi». **How the three lines divide into two witnesses is not certain**: the clerk writes «*Pasquale Lau=/dato, di Antonio/ Crisci*» with no conjunction, and it may be one man «Pasquale Laudato di Antonio» and a second surnamed Crisci. **Left as it reads.**

SABATINO'S FATHER, AND A GENERATION THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. «*figlio di **fu CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, di professione **contadino***» — dead before January 1860, of Forchia. **NOT the Carmine Annecchino who married Maria Carfora and fathered Filomena in 1897**; that one was bearing children from 1883 and is two generations later. **The name recurs in this family**, which is worth holding onto rather than resolving.
«*e di **ROSA CEGLIA defunta***» — Sabatino Annecchino's mother, dead before January 1860. **CEGLIA HAS NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE**, under any spelling.

«*MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA, di anni **ventinove**, **nata in ARIENZO***» — so born about 1831, and **an Arienzo woman, not a Forchia one**. This archive had her only as a mother of four daughters born 1861–1866.

**MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA'S FATHER — AND HE WAS ALIVE, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAD SAID HE WAS NOT.** «*figlia di **VALERIO CARFORA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi***» — and **there the sentence stops**. The act writes «**defunto**» after Carmine Annecchino, «**defunta**» after Rosa Ceglia and «**defunta**» after Pasqua Morgillo. **It writes nothing after him.** **And the act proves it a second time, in its own list of documents.** Item **6** of the eight papers read into the marriage is «*Nel **CONSENSO DEL PADRE** della stessa, **dato nell'atto***» — the bride's father consented **in person, in the act**, on 21 January 1860. **A dead man does not consent.** **THE FORENAME RESOLVES, AND IT WAS NEVER ILLEGIBLE — IT WAS SPLIT.** This archive recorded «*the word reads «[L/t]erio» at four times magnification and is left unread rather than guessed*». **The word is not one word.** It wraps across the column: the line ends «*figlia di **Va***» and the next begins «***lerio** Carfora*». **VALERIO** — and no other Italian forename ends in *-lerio*. **The archive magnified the second half of a word and called the whole of it illegible.** **So the Carfora are an Arienzo family as well as a Forchia one**, and **Valerio Carfora, contadino of Arienzo, was living there in January 1860** — a man to look for, not a death to look for.

«*e di **PASQUA MORGILLO defunta***» — Maria Antonia Carfora's mother, **dead before 21 January 1860**, and the only one of the bride's two parents the act does mark. **A CARFORA–MORGILLO marriage at Arienzo**, in the generation born about 1800. **Her death act is in the marriage's own dossier**: item **7** of the eight documents read into the act is «*Nell'atto di morte della madre della stessa*». **The Arienzo processetto for 1860 would hand over the date, the street and her parents in one page.**

A CHILD OF GENERATION THREE THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **STANISLAO FALCO**, di anni **VENTIQUATTRO**, nato in **ARIENZO**, di professione **PASTORE**, domiciliato in Arienzo, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in Arienzo, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata ivi; e **FILOMENA DI LUCIA**, di anni ventitré, nata in Arienzo, figlia di fu [?] di Lucia, **muratore**, e di **MARTA di NIZZO***». Church celebration **23 September 1861**, parish of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**. **A PASTORE — a shepherd — in a house of contadini.** Twenty-four in September 1861 gives **b. c.1837**, which would make Andreana Crisci about forty at his birth: late, but this register's ages are good to about three years and no better, and she was bearing children into 1828 on the archive's own reckoning.

ALIVE AT SIXTY-NINE, three years before the other sighting. «*figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **Arienzo***» — **no «fu», no «defunto»**, in an act that marks the bride's father dead in the very next clause («*figlia di **fu** [?] di Lucia*»).

«*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***» — alive, unmarked, on the same evidence. This is the Andreana Crisci who married Vincenzo Falco in December 1814, not the other woman of the name this archive keeps separate.

Stanislao Falco's bride: **twenty-three**, born Arienzo, so b. c.1838. **Her parents are LUIGI DI LUCIA, *muratore*, and MARTA DI NIZZO** — the father's forename is illegible on the marriage act itself and comes from the **NOTIFICAZIONI register bound into the same volume**, which gives the same couple in a clerk's cleaner hand: «*matrimonio tra **STANISLAO FALCO** figlio di **VINCENZO** e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, e **FILOMENA DI LUCIA** figlia di **LUIGI** e di **MARTA DI NIZZO***». Her father was already dead at the wedding. Her father is a ***muratore*** — a mason, **a lettered-adjacent trade in this corpus**, where nearly every man is a contadino, colono or bracciale.

THE REGISTER ACT BEHIND THE INDEX ENTRY. Act 14: «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANDREA FALCO maggiore**, di anni **VENTIQUATTRO**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato ivi, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, di professione **FILATRICE**, domiciliata ivi; e **MARIA CARMELA BUONO maggiore**, di anni ventiquattro, di professione filatrice, nata in Arienzo, domiciliata in **strada Porta di Sopra***». Church **24 May 1846** at Sant'Andrea, which is the date the index gave. Witnesses Agostino di Giglio and **Gennaro Laudato**. **TWENTY-FOUR IN MAY 1846 GIVES b. c.1822** — four years before Angelandrea, and the two are separate men on the ages alone.

**«MINORE» — AND THAT ONE WORD CONFIRMS HIS BIRTH ACT.** Act on img4r: «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANGELANDREA FALCO MINORE**, di anni **venti[…]**, nato in Arienzo, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, **colono**, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, **filatrice** … e **MARIA CIMMINO maggiore** … nata in Arienzo, domiciliata in **strada Capodiconca**, figlia di **ALESSANDRO CIMMINO**, contadino*». Church **29 March 1847** at Sant'Andrea. Witnesses **Gennaro Laudato** and Francesco de Angelis. **MAJORITY WAS TWENTY-ONE**, so «minore» puts him under it — and his birth act of **12 September 1826** makes him twenty years and six months. The numeral itself carries a flourish and is not read beyond «venti[…]»; **the word «minore» is what bounds him, and it is unambiguous.** **A DATE CONFLICT, RECORDED NOT RESOLVED:** this archive also holds «Angelo Falco … m. Maria Cimmino» on **17 April 1847** from a parish ark — the same bride, three weeks later. Both are kept. **AND THE ACT'S OWN INDICAZIONE COLUMN SETTLES THE CHURCH DATE, READ 20 SEPTEMBER 2026**: «*Il Parroco di SANT'ANDREA … ha certificato, che la celebrazione del matrimonio è seguita nel giorno **VENTINOVE** del mese di MARZO anno corrente*» — the priest's own certificate, copied into the register, spelling the day out in words. **The same day as the civil promise.** The index's date was read here as «24 MARZO» and it is 29; under this system the church cannot precede the promise, so a 24 was impossible on its face. For contrast, act 20 of 1848 in the next volume has the promise on **19 August** and the church on **23 August** — four days later, which is the usual shape.

A SIGHTING IN THE 1844–1861 GAP. «*figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **COLONO**, domiciliato ivi*» — no «fu», in an act whose own next clause marks the bride's father when he is dead. Named the same way again on 29 March 1847.

**HER TRADE, FOR THE FIRST TIME: FILATRICE — a spinner.** «*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, di professione **filatrice**, domiciliata ivi*». Alive and unmarked, and given the same way again on 29 March 1847. This archive had her age five times and her occupation never.

Andrea Falco's bride: twenty-four, **filatrice**, born Arienzo, of **strada Porta di Sopra**, daughter of **ONOFRIO BUONO** and **ANGELA IMBIMBO** — the parents from the index, now with her own age, trade and street. **Verified against the image, work-list row 58 — act 14, folio 187, before TOMASO ANZEVINO Sindaco — and the act gives her father two things the index did not.** «*figlia di **ONOFRIO BUONO Defunto**, di professione **BARBIERE**, domiciliato ivi, e di **ANGELICA IMBIMBO**, di professione filatrice, domiciliata ivi*». **He was a BARBER and he was already DEAD** in May 1846. **And her mother's forename is ANGELICA, not «Angela»** — the act's own form. The church celebration followed on **24 May** before **AGOSTINO DI GIGLIO** and **GENNARO LAUDATO**.

**HER FORENAME AT LAST — CAMILLA.** The index gave only «*CARBONE […]*», which is why this household carries a bracket in its name. The register act reads «*e di **CAMILLA CARBONE detta […]**, di professione **FILATRICE**, domiciliata ivi*» — **and she carries a «detta» alias that does not resolve.** She is alive in August 1848; her husband **PIETRO FALCO** is «**defunto**». **NO KINSHIP TO THIS LINE IS CLAIMED**: the patria is AIROLA.

THE REGISTER ACT BEHIND THE INDEX. Act 20, civil **19 August 1848**, church **23 August** at Sant'Andrea — the index's date. «*FRANCESCO FALCO maggiore, di anni **trentuno**, **nato in AIROLA**, di professione contadino … figlio di **PIETRO FALCO DEFUNTO** … e di **CAMILLA CARBONE** … e **GIUSEPPA RIVETTI MINORE**, di anni ventisei, contadina, **nata in Arienzo***». Witnesses **Alfonso Verdicchio** and **Salvatore Laudato**. **Thirty-one in 1848 gives b. c.1817.** The bride's parents are **GIOVANNI RIVETTI and [—] ALTARELLI**, exactly as the index read them. **Still no kinship claimed to this line.**

«*è comparso **ANIELLO CARFORA**, di anni **trentuno**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in questo Comune **STRADA CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **Maschio***» — atto of 10 January 1831. **A CARFORA HOUSEHOLD ON THE FALCO'S OWN STREET**, thirty years before the marriage act that first told this archive the Carfora were an Arienzo family at all. Thirty-one here, so born about 1800 — the same generation as «[?]erio Carfora», Maria Antonia's father. **He is not that man**: this one's wife is Orsola Porrino. THIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOT JOINED TO ANY OTHER IN THIS ARCHIVE. It is recorded because work-list row 63 asked whether the Carfora were an Arienzo family at all, and the answer is that they were — three separate Carfora households appear in a single year of one register. Whether any of them is the house of «[?]erio Carfora and Pasqua Morgillo» is NOT established and is not claimed. **Verified against the image, work-list row 58 — and the act has a number this archive never recorded: it is ATTO 6.** The parish named in the second column is **SANT'ANDREA APOSTOLO DI ARIENZO**. The witness to the presentation is **MARCELLO RIVETTI, forty-eight**, contadino — a Rivetti of the right generation on the Falco's street, recorded and not claimed.

evidence: **THE MARGIN OF HER BIRTH ACT CARRIES HER WEDDING, TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER.** Written vertically down the left edge: «*(1) **a 10 Ottobre 1874** l'Uff[icial]e dello Stato Civile d'**Arienzo** sposò **DOMENICA FALCO** con **PASQUA[LE]…ANTONIO GUIDA***», and beneath it the registrar's own dating, «*Caserta **31 Luglio 1884***». **The husband's forename is cut by the binding** — «Pasqua…» on one line and «…lantonio» on the next, so **Pasqualantonio**, the Neapolitan compound — but **GUIDA is clear**, and the tree had already called her «Domenica Falco (Guida)» from nothing but family memory. **THIS IS A MARRIAGE OF 1874, IN A SERIES ANTENATI STOPS FILMING IN 1865.** The margin reaches nine years past the end of the registers. **AND THERE IS A SECOND MARGIN ON THE SAME ACT, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAD NOT READ.** In the right-hand column, below the registrar's signature: «*(1) **A 25 Marzo 1881** l'Uff.le dello Stato Civ.le d'**ARIENZO** sposò **DOMENICA FALCO** con **PASQUALE SACCAVINO*** — **Caserta 16 Giugno 1884***». **SHE MARRIED TWICE.** The first margin, down the left edge, gives **10 October 1874** and **Pasqualantonio Guida**; this one gives **25 March 1881** and **PASQUALE SACCAVINO**, dated at Caserta seven weeks before the other. **So Pasqualantonio Guida died between October 1874 and March 1881**. **One birth act, two marriages, both after the year Antenati stops filming the series.** The margin method reaches **thirty-five years** past the register it is written in — and the second margin was on the page the whole time this archive was quoting the first.

evidence: THE ONLY AUTOGRAPH OF ANYONE IN THIS LINE. At the foot of notarial act 85 the notary writes «quindi si è firmato soltanto il detto PASQUALE FALCO, avendo la detta CHIARA RIVETTI dichiarato di NON SAPERE SCRIVERE» — and below it, in a large, slow, unjoined hand quite unlike the notary's, stands «PASCALE FALCO». THE DATE IS 8 SEPTEMBER 1814, NOT 8 DECEMBER: the act is headed «Il giorno OTTO 8 del Mese di SETTEMBRE dell'Anno Milleottocento, e quattordici 1814», and the registration endorsement at its foot reads «Reg[istra]to in Arienzo li DODICI SETTEMBRE 1814». Consent on 8 September, banns on 11 and 18 September, marriage on 15 October — the sequence only closes once the December is gone.

evidence: «*assistita da **BRIGIDA COSSI** sua madre di anni **CINQUANTASEI**, di professione **contadina**, domiciliata colla figlia*» — born about 1759, a widow giving consent for a daughter who was still a minor. **The surname is COSSI and this one is worth the space.** This archive has spent months correcting *Cossi* to *Cioffi* on strada Camellara, on a test about the descender of the doubled letter. **That test does not work in this hand**: read at twelve times, the doubled letters here descend exactly as a double f would, and so do the ones in «MASSONE» and «SANSONE», which are certainly long ſ. **What separates the two names is the letter count**: *Cioffi* carries an **i between the C and the o** and *Cossi* does not. There is no such i here, in this act or in act 21 of the same volume, where **ELISABETTA COSSI** and her father **MARINO COSSI** are written the same way. **Cossi is a real Arienzo surname**, and the Camellara correction was about one household, not about the name.

evidence: A DATE FOR A BAPTISM THIS ARCHIVE COULD NOT DATE. «*è morto nella propria casa **PASQUALE DI GUIDA d'anni CINQUANTASETTE**, marito di [forename unread], nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **SENSALE**, domiciliato ivi, **figlio di GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato ivi, **e di MADDALENA RIVETTA Defunta**, domiciliata ivi*» — act 50 of 11 August 1836, at twenty hours. **He is a brother of ANTONIA DI GUIDA**, generation four's mother-in-law, on the same two parents the 1802 marriage act gives her. This archive held him only as a parish baptism of **31 January, year unread**; his trade, his death and a stated age are new. **THE STATED AGE DOES NOT FIT THE OBVIOUS YEAR AND IS NOT FORCED TO.** Fifty-seven in August 1836 implies about **1779** — but this household baptised a **Margherita on 14 March 1779**, six weeks after a 31 January, so the two cannot both be 1779. Either his baptism is 31 January of another year, or the register is guessing his age, which it demonstrably does. The age is recorded as the register's, not as a birth year. **And the father is NOT marked defunto while the mother is** — which this archive does not read as proof he was living, for the reason set out on /corrections.

evidence: «*sono comparsi **CLEMENTE DI GUIDA** di anni **trentatré**, di professione **SENSALE**, regnicolo, domiciliato in strada Maddalena*» — born about 1803, and of the dead man's own trade. **A di Guida declaring a di Guida death is the register's usual mark of close kin**, but the act assigns him no relationship word and none is claimed. The second declarant is **CARLANTONIO MORGILLO, fifty, contadino, of strada CAMELLARA** — the Falco's own street, and the second man of that name this archive keeps apart from the Carlantonio Morgillo who married Rosa Falco in 1802.

evidence: **THE SECOND DOCUMENT THIS HOUSEHOLD HAS EVER HAD, AND ITS FIRST CHILD.** «*la stessa è nata da **GIOVANNA FALCO, di anni VENTOTTO**, domiciliata in **strada CRISCI**, e da **ANIELLO CRISCI marito della stessa, di anni VENTISEI, di professione CONTADINO**, domiciliato con detta sua moglie, nel giorno **VENTOTTO** del mese di **GIUGNO**, anno corrente, alle ore **TREDICI**, nella casa propria di detti conjugi … il nome di **PASQUALINA***». Witnessed by **ANGELO MIGLIORE**, forty-three, *sartore* of strada Croce dell'Ospedale, and **CLEMENTE CRISCI**, twenty-eight, *calzolajo*. The couple married on **6 September 1829**; this child comes two years and nine months later. **Giovanna Falco is a daughter of GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA**, so Pasqualina is a granddaughter of the founder's son. Her mother's stated age of twenty-eight puts her birth about 1804.

evidence: **A CHILD BORN THE DAY BEFORE HER PARENTS' WEDDING.** «*la stessa è nata da **MARIA RAFFAELA FALCO, di anni DICIOTTO**, domiciliata in **strada CAMELLARA**, e da **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO marito della stessa, di anni VENTISEI, di professione CONTADINO**, domiciliato con detta sua moglie, nel giorno **QUINDICI** del mese di **LUGLIO**, anno corrente, alle ore **CINQUE E MEZZA**, nella casa propria di detti conjugi … il nome di **MARIA CARMELA***». Witnessed by **FRANCESCO MACCHIA**, thirty-three, of strada Capodiconca, and **PIETRO VERDICCHIO**, sixty. **This archive dates the marriage of Francescantonio Falco and Raffaela Falco to 16 JULY 1832**, from the marriage index — the day AFTER this birth. The act nevertheless calls him «**marito della stessa**», which is consistent: a birth act is drawn a day or two after the birth, by which time they were married. **Neither date is adjusted to suit the other.** The index date is a church date and has not been read against the civil act. Her mother's stated eighteen puts her birth about 1814; her own death act of 1854 makes her thirty-four, which puts it about 1820. The registers guess.

evidence: **AND THIS ONE BEARS ON THE DISTINCTION THIS ARCHIVE DREW ON 20 SEPTEMBER.** «*la stessa è nata da **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA, di anni VENTOTTO**, domiciliata in **strada CAMELLARA**, e da **MICHELANGELO FALCO marito della stessa, di anni VENTISEI, di professione CONTADINO**, domiciliato con detta sua moglie, nel giorno **VENTI** del mese di **LUGLIO**, anno corrente, alle ore **UNDICI**, nella casa propria di detti conjugi … il nome di **MARIA ROSA***». Witnessed by **VINCENZO DIGLIO**, thirty-two, of strada Santa Lucia, and **PASQUALE DI RUSSO**, twenty-eight. **This archive files a MARIA ROSA FALCO who died on 30 May 1834 under «Michele Falco & Antonia Vigliotta»** — the other man. Born 20 July 1832, she would be one year and ten months old at that death, which fits. **Either the 1834 act belongs to MICHELANGELO's daughter and the household assignment is wrong, or there were two Maria Rosa Falco of two men whose names and whose wives' names both nearly coincide.** The birth act says MICHELANGELO, in full, twice. **Nothing is moved on the strength of it**: the 1834 death act has not been re-read, and that is the test. See /open-questions.

evidence: **ACT 108, AND THE CHILD WAS BAPTISED THE SAME DAY.** «*L'anno mille ottocento **trentasette**, il dì **trentuno** del mese di **AGOSTO**, alle ore dodici, avanti di noi **ELIA COLETTA Sindaco** … è comparso **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO, di anni TRENTUNO, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in STRADA CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **RAFFAELA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni VENTISEI** … nel giorno **TRENTUNO** del mese di **Agosto**, anno corrente, **alle ore SEI**, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione … il nome di **RAFFAELE***». Witnessed by **VINCENZO MAURO**, forty-two, *vaticale* of strada Croce dell'Ospedale, and **ORAZIO MORGILLO**, forty-two, *colono*. The INDICAZIONE column records the **Parroco di SANT'ANDREA APOSTOLO** returning the notice on the **thirty-first of August**, so he was baptised on the day he was born. **A SIXTH child for the first-cousin marriage**, beside Carmina (d. 1832), **MARIA CARMELA (b. 15 July 1832)**, Pasqualina (d. 1836), Pasquale (b. 1838) and Clemente (d. 1853). **And the mother's age moves again**: twenty-six here implies about 1811, eighteen in July 1832 implies about 1814, and her death act of 1854 makes her thirty-four, implying about 1820. **Three documents, three birth years, nine years apart.** None is adopted.

evidence: **AN EIGHTH CHILD FOR A HOUSEHOLD WHOSE CHILDREN KEPT DYING, AND THE FIRST RECORD IT HAS FOR 1833.** Act 85: «*L'anno mille ottocento **trentatre**, il dì **ventitre** del mese di **AGOSTO**, ad ore dodici, avanti di noi **FRANCESCO D'AMBROSIO Sindaco** … è comparso **FRANCESCO C[OSSI/CIOFFI], di anni QUARANTA, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in STRADA CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTADUE** … nel giorno **VENTITRE** del mese di Agosto, anno corrente, **alle ore DIECI**, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione … il nome di **CLEMENTE***». Witnessed by **AGOSTINO ARRIGALE**, fifty, *vaticale* of strada Capodiconca, and **PELLEGRINO VIGLIOTTA**, thirty. The INDICAZIONE records the **Parroco di SANT'ANDREA APOSTOLO** returning the notice on the **twenty-seventh of August**, so he was baptised four days after his birth. **THE FATHER'S SURNAME IS NOT LEGIBLE ENOUGH IN THIS HAND TO TOUCH THE STANDING CORRECTION, AND IT IS NOT TOUCHED.** This archive corrected this household from *Cossi* to **CIOFFI** from the 1825 register at full resolution, and that correction stands. Read here at 3,200 pixels the surname shows a large flourished **C**, a round **o**, a doubled letter with long descenders and a final **i** — which by the letter-count test would be *Cossi*, **except that the C's own flourish could conceal the i that makes it Cioffi**. *At this resolution, in this hand, the two cannot be separated* — which is what this archive said when it first met the problem: «at plate resolution the two surnames are not distinguishable; go to the image». **Here even the image is marginal.** The household keeps the name the 1825 act gave it. **Maria Falco is thirty-two**, which puts her birth about 1801.

evidence: **AND THIS ONE THE EARLIER SWEEP OF THIS VOLUME COULD NOT HAVE FOUND.** Act 71: «*L'anno mille ottocento **trentuno**, il dì **OTTO** del mese di **AGOSTO**, ad ore undici, avanti di noi **DON ANDREA LORIA Secondo eletto** … è comparso **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, di anni TRENTASEI, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **MARIA FALCO sua moglie legitima, di anni TRENTACINQUE** … nel giorno **OTTO** del mese di Agosto, anno corrente, **alle ore QUATTRO** … il nome di **ANTONIA***». Witnessed by **CESARE DIGLIO**, forty-six, *contadino* **of strada Camellara**, and **RAFFAELE ZUFFARELLA**, forty. Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo d'Arienzo the same day**. **THE SURNAME IS PLAIN HERE, AND IT CONFIRMS THE 1825 CORRECTION FROM A THIRD ACT**: *C-i-o-ff-i*, with the **i between the C and the o** that a *Cossi* does not have. The 1833 act of this same household is written in a worse hand where the two cannot be separated; this one can. **SHE IS THE SECOND ANTONIA.** The first died on **20 June 1823**. This household also buried a **Mariantonia on 23 October 1828** and another **Mariantonia on 3 December 1832** — and **that last one may be this child**, sixteen months old. *It is not claimed*: the 1832 death act has not been re-read, and a household that reuses a dead child's name three times is exactly the one where a join like that must be proved rather than assumed.

evidence: **AND THIS ONE PROBABLY DATES A DEATH THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD.** Act 74: «*L'anno mille ottocento **ventinove**, il dì **CINQUE** del mese di **OTTOBRE**, ad ore ventitré … è comparso **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, di anni TRENTASEI, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA FALCO sua moglie legitima, di anni TRENTAQUATTRO** … nel giorno **CINQUE** del mese di Ottobre, anno corrente, **alle ore QUINDICI**, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione … il nome di **GIUSEPPE***». Witnessed by **VINCENZO DIGLIO**, thirty-five, of strada Sant'Andrea, and **LORENZO LIPARULO**, forty-five. Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo the following day**. **This archive holds a GIUSEPPE CIOFFI «the second» who died on 5 December 1830.** Born 5 October 1829 he would be **fourteen months old** at that death, which fits, and the household's first Giuseppe died on 25 March 1824. **The join is likely and is not claimed**: the 1830 death act has not been re-read. **Maria Falco is thirty-four here, thirty-five two years later in 1831, and thirty-two four years later in 1833.** Her husband is thirty-six in 1829 and thirty-six again in 1831. The register is guessing both of them.
